newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on central bank support.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on central bank support.

text.p: The won ended up on Thursday after the central bank's dollar-selling intervention underlined its intention to support the local currency, dealers said.
Dealers said the Bank of Korea intervened in the early morning and afternoon, at around 854.70 won and 853.50-854.50. The bank has never acknowledged stepping into the market.
The won ended at 853.70 after opening at an 83-month low of 855.00. It touched an intraday high of 852.50.
"Until importer positions are all digested, it will be difficult for the won to rise," said a local bank dealer.
Another domestic bank trader said there was demand for about $250 million in the market.
Dealers said the won was being hit by the economic slowdown, heavy import settlements, and the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen on world markets.
The dollar hit a 47-month high of 119.30 yen in early trading in Tokyo.
The won was expected to come under further pressure on Friday and test the 855 level again. The won's base mid-rate was pegged at 854.10 for Friday, against 853.60 on Thursday.
